domain_reasoning: Most time goes into opening the case and entering the remedy in billing, order or payment systems.
length_reasoning: A simple refund takes a few minutes of lookup and entry; an exchange or multi-line bill adjustment with notes takes half an hour.
review_reasoning: A supervisor or finance reviewer checks the entry against the decided remedy and the case note; larger adjustments need more lines traced.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong amount or account causes a payment error that is usually caught and reversed, but large ones are real money loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's refund rules, billing system and approval limits, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Besides talking, the time goes into entering the order or cancellation in the order or account system.
length_reasoning: A simple order or cancellation takes a few minutes; one with retention offers, multiple items or payment problems takes a quarter of an hour.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the recorded contact and checks the order or cancellation record for accuracy.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong order or missed cancellation causes a complaint and a correction or refund, but is reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's products, order system and cancellation policies, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written diagnosis, produced by reading notes and logs and writing it up.
length_reasoning: A short write-up of a clear problem takes about twenty minutes; a complex multi-cause diagnosis with evidence takes a couple of hours.
review_reasoning: A developer or customer reads it and checks the reasoning and evidence against the product; complex ones need the logs checked.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong diagnosis sends developers or the customer the wrong way, costing rework, but is caught when the fix fails.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and the customer's setup, built over weeks.

unit_flag_reason: One vacancy mixes screening, interviewing and deciding over days or weeks, and hiring is only loosely part of a support specialist's work.
domain_reasoning: Reviewing applications, interviewing and writing recommendations is mostly reading and writing.
length_reasoning: Active time covers screening a stack of applications, several interviews and the recommendation, spread over days.
review_reasoning: HR or the hiring manager checks the shortlist, interview notes and the reasoning behind the pick.
stakes_reasoning: A bad hire is costly but reversible within probation; a wrong pick for a critical role is costly.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the team's needs and the company's hiring process, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is operating installers, settings and tools on the user's machine.
length_reasoning: A standard install follows a checklist in minutes; a repair that needs troubleshooting or several reboots takes over an hour.
review_reasoning: The support lead or user confirms the software runs and the ticket is closed; the check is quick.
stakes_reasoning: A bad install is noticed by the user quickly and redone, though a conflicting patch can break a machine.
context_reasoning: A skilled outsider could follow the specification, with only a little local tool knowledge.

domain_reasoning: The evaluator mostly operates the software at the site and observes it, then notes findings.
length_reasoning: A short remote evaluation takes a couple of hours; an on-site visit with travel-free active work and a full write-up takes most of two days.
review_reasoning: The test lead reads the findings and checks key observations against logs or the objectives; long evaluations need more checking.
stakes_reasoning: Missed or wrong findings lead to wrong product decisions or bugs reaching release, but this is generally caught later.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and the beta customer's environment, built over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The time goes into monitoring tools, logs and profilers.
length_reasoning: Many anomalies are explained quickly; a real performance problem can take hours of tracing.
review_reasoning: A lead reads the findings and checks the evidence against monitoring data; deep investigations need the reasoning followed.
stakes_reasoning: Wrongly closing a real issue can let a slowdown or outage reach users, though most are caught on recurrence.
context_reasoning: Telling a real anomaly from noise needs months of knowing this system's normal behaviour.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into entering the remedy in billing or order systems.
length_reasoning: A simple refund is entered in a couple of minutes; an exchange or larger adjustment with an approval takes longer.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the contact and checks the entry matches what was agreed.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong entry causes a money error or complaint, usually reversible; larger adjustments are costlier.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's refund rules, limits and systems, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Entries are written into a log or ticketing tool as text throughout the day.
length_reasoning: Active time is the writing of entries, spread through the day; a quiet day is short, a busy install day is long.
review_reasoning: A supervisor skims the log for completeness; an auditor-level check traces some entries to tickets.
stakes_reasoning: A poor log is noticed at audit or when someone needs the history, with limited immediate harm.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's log conventions and systems, picked up over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading logs, configuration and code.
length_reasoning: Obvious failures take minutes; hard ones with unclear logs take a few hours.
review_reasoning: A developer reads the stated source and checks it against the logs or config cited.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong guess wastes developer time but is caught when they start work.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of this code base and system behaviour, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The work is installing and configuring tools, which is configuration work.
length_reasoning: A simple upgrade takes half an hour; a new tool integrated with CI and accounts takes most of a day.
review_reasoning: A QA lead confirms the tool works by running a sample test and checking configuration.
stakes_reasoning: A broken tool disrupts the team but is noticed quickly and fixed.
context_reasoning: Needs familiarity with the team's environments and pipeline, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is matching records and creating the invoice in the billing system.
length_reasoning: A simple single-line return takes a few minutes; a partial shipment with price discrepancies takes most of an hour.
review_reasoning: Billing checks the invoice against the requisition and original invoice line by line.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong credit goes to the customer and accounts, reversible but sometimes large money.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's invoicing and returns rules and systems, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is running commands and tools and reading output.
length_reasoning: A short check of a few systems takes ten minutes; a large estate with follow-up tickets takes an hour.
review_reasoning: A supervisor checks the record against the systems and that errors became tickets; thorough checks re-run some commands.
stakes_reasoning: A missed error usually shows later, but one that is missed can become an outage.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of what is normal on these systems, built over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is setting up and running tests across configurations.
length_reasoning: A small matrix takes a couple of hours; a wide matrix with many environments takes most of two days.
review_reasoning: A lead checks the matrix coverage, results and filed issues; large cycles need more sampling.
stakes_reasoning: Missed incompatibilities reach users and cause complaints or patches, and a release problem can be costly.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and supported environments, built over weeks.

domain_reasoning: A test plan is a written document drawn up from requirements.
length_reasoning: A small change needs a short plan in a couple of hours; a full release plan takes much of two days.
review_reasoning: The test lead and team read the plan and check it against the requirements; larger plans need coverage checked.
stakes_reasoning: A weak plan lets defects through but gaps are usually spotted as testing proceeds.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and the team's test process, built over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written how-to guide, with screenshots and steps.
length_reasoning: A short procedure takes about an hour; a guide for a new system takes several hours.
review_reasoning: The supervisor reads it and tries the steps to check them.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong step confuses users and creates tickets, but is fixed quickly.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the company's systems and users, but the steps can be followed by an outsider.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into completing the order forms in the system.
length_reasoning: A simple address change takes a few minutes; a new contract or discontinuance with checks takes longer.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the contact and checks the submitted order against what was requested.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong order causes a service or billing error that the customer reports and is reversed, but a wrong discontinuance can be costly.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's forms, systems and policies, learned over weeks.
